recent_decisions.decision: Step B (who can reach me, design 10c) merged from three parallel worktrees: relay (reach_settings table, reach_set/reach_settings/reach_refused, enforcement at dm_put, voice_call and its signals, trade_request and dc_offer, the groups audience, open calls tracked in memory as a hash of the two keys, contact requests 5 a day), desktop (Settings > Safety, People who may call me re-issuing passes, refusal notice, Requests list), web (the mirror, plus window.peerData exposed so names resolve). Safe defaults: messages friends, calls chosen, trades friends; admins bound.
recent_decisions.why: The operator: safe by default, choose individuals for calls. The web build found the first contact-request design could never form a friendship under the defaults and could be spoofed (256 bytes cannot hold a signature); amended mid-build so a request is an ordinary signed sealed DM carrying the requester s pass, and the accepter s reply attaches it, keeping the relay free of who-asked-whom records. The relay build found the 256-byte rule could never have worked anyway (every signed DM pads to 16,384).

recent_decisions.decision: Step C (Block, design 10d) merged from two parallel worktrees and released as v0.1468.0: Block by key withdraws your passes and unfollows locally, hides the person on every client path, syncs devices by a sealed note to yourself ([[hum:block:v1]] / [[hum:unblock:v1]], identical on both clients, checked by a Node test reading the Rust constants), Settings > Safety > Blocked people. Also fixed: BUG-175 (web server list fetch loop), the flaky reach-web test. Docs: conformance_gaps marks the contact-consent gap closed with its remaining limits; the Accord chapter note and the conflict guide rewritten; Library resynced.
recent_decisions.why: The operator: give users the tools to protect themselves. The three Block decisions (local unfollow, note format, their pass kept) were settled by the web build and sent to the desktop build mid-flight so both clients match. Remaining limits stated publicly rather than hidden: under Anyone a blocked person still reaches the mailbox, public posts stay visible, game nameplates not yet hidden.

recent_decisions.decision: Step D (reports the admins can check, design 10e) merged from three parallel worktrees, released as v0.1469.0: report_v2 signed by the reporter over a pinned preimage with a BLAKE3 evidence hash; DM evidence checked by the relay against the target signature over the DM v2 inner words; posts looked up; group text unproven; Reports for admins and mods (mods never see the reporter); decisions through the moderation rules; 90-day cull after decision. Also the outside-help findings (18 countries, dated, quoted), the desktop built-in copy of report_reasons.json, and moderators spelled either way see Reports.
recent_decisions.why: The operator: protect the users. A web builder noticed a DM carrying an encrypted file holds its key in the text; a report could hand an admin the means to open abuse imagery, which is itself a crime to view or pass on. Since the signature covers the text, such messages can never be evidence: refused by the relay and offered by neither client (marker matched in any version). The underlying legal duties of a server operator on such a report are logged in PRIORITIES for a dated findings document.

recent_decisions.decision: Step E (our own STUN and the room-scoped call forwarder, design 10f) merged from three parallel worktrees, released as v0.1470.0: one UDP port with a rate-limited STUN responder and a closed TURN forwarder whose relayed addresses are virtual and which delivers only between allocations of the same room; call_credentials over the signed-in socket; both clients connect calls and rooms relay only, Google removed everywhere (a native lint scans src, web and app/web), group mesh and contact channels off, direct offers answered only from own devices.
recent_decisions.why: The operator approved it (Do we have to go through Google? and Let us do this). The forwarder cannot reach any outside address, which is what made the 2026-08-07 reflector possible. Calls stay unavailable, said plainly, until the operator opens UDP 3478 with the command in docs/admin/call-forwarder.md; the AI does not change firewall settings.

recent_decisions.decision: Step F (warnings and the recovery-phrase guard, design 10g) merged from two parallel worktrees (web chat, desktop app), released as v0.1471.0: warnings under direct and group messages matched from data/safety/warnings.json by one normalising rule on both clients (Unicode \p{Alphabetic}\p{N} on web equals Rust char::is_alphanumeric, 17 shared cases in scripts/tests/fixtures/warning-cases.json), a stranger's links held until Open, and a send holding 4 or more of the sender's own recovery-phrase words in a row stopped with no send-anyway. Number-only words are now left out before the run check, so a phrase pasted as a numbered list is stopped too (found by the desktop agent). Reported posts show admins neither a file nor a link (relay without_files_or_links).
recent_decisions.why: The operator asked for tools that protect people from scams and predators, for everyone and not only children. Warnings are checked on the device only, because messages are end-to-end encrypted and nobody, admins included, can read them. The numbered-list gap mattered because backup screens show the phrase numbered, which is exactly how people copy it. The admin redaction follows the 2026-10-10 report-duties finding: a reported post must never put abuse material in front of an admin.

recent_decisions.decision: Step B and D follow-ups built on both clients from four parallel worktrees and released as v0.1472.0: 10c-ii, a Message, Call and Trade tick per friend on "People I choose" (the pass carries message+invite+voice_message, trade, call; invite alone when nothing is ticked, because the format refuses an empty may), and 10e-ii, help outside this server in the report dialog (emergency number, also lines, the child-report body, a country the person picks, kept on the device, never sent, https links only). recent_decisions.why: The operator asked to choose individuals who may message or call; until 10c-ii "People I choose" only worked for calls. The help lines follow the dated outside-help finding. Building web and desktop against one written spec, then having the second builder match the first one's choices, kept the two apps saying the same words.

recent_decisions.decision: Two dated findings written before the protected setup: children's online-safety rules (COPPA and the FTC Act, US states, UK Children's code and Online Safety Act, EU DSA and GDPR) and California AB 1043 as rewritten by AB 1856 (in force 1 January 2027). Spec 10h (step G, the protected setup) written from them, with every on-screen word in data/gui/safety_presets.json; web and desktop builders dispatched. Three operator decisions recorded in PRIORITIES: the age position (the web chat says 18 or older), content rules on the project server's rules page, and whether to email the FTC COPPA hotline.
recent_decisions.why: CLAUDE.md requires a dated primary-source finding before any "for children" claim. The finding says nothing forbids a parent's PIN lock and nothing supports "kid safe" or "compliant"; the FTC has acted on parental-control claims with gaps (Messenger Kids), so 10h adds a review of existing friends, groups and rooms when the setup is turned on, and an always-visible line telling the person it is on (ICO standard 11). AB 1043 now forbids asking the operating system for an age when not required, so the setup never asks, and a store listing needs a decision first.

recent_decisions.decision: Step G, the protected setup (spec 10h), built on both clients from parallel worktrees and released as v0.1473.0, with every on-screen word in data/gui/safety_presets.json (sentences, lines and 26 labels). Review and alignment after the merge: the web added PIN gates for every copy of the identity (encrypted backup, identity file, device-link code, onboarding phrase step, the settings page); the desktop gained the same gate on its device-link QR; "Forgot the PIN?" got one rule on both apps (a recorded identity must match; a missing or malformed one, which only damage leaves, falls back to the identity in use); a mention in a hidden room no longer dings. BUG-176 found by reading the report dialog's snapshot: v0.1472.0's desktop report dialog hid Send; new widgets::dialog_scrolling.
recent_decisions.why: The operator asked for a mode that protects kids from predators and scams. The dated finding set the words (never "kid safe" or "compliant") and the shape (review existing contacts, tell the person, no flag sent anywhere). Fail-closed on a damaged identity was rejected because it would lock a damaged setup for good (on the web, clearing site data, identity and all, would be the only way out). BUG-176 shipped because every test passed and nobody read the rendered dialog; the lesson went into BUGS.md and the UI-verification memory.

recent_decisions.decision: Spec 10i built on the relay and both clients from three parallel worktrees and released as v0.1474.0: an admin or the owner erases another person's data with the person's name typed to confirm. The relay factored the self-erase into one shared function (handlers/account_erase.rs carry_out) both erases call; AccountErased gained by_admin; admin_erase_done carries the receipt; the log names nobody. Moderators cannot erase; admins and the owner cannot be erased this way. The public roadmap also gained the safety work.
recent_decisions.why: The children's online-safety finding (judgement call 7): an operator who learns a member is under 13 is expected to delete the child's information, and only a person could erase their own data. One shared function keeps the admin erase from ever doing less than the self-erase.

recent_decisions.decision: Spec 10j built (relay, then web first, then desktop matching the web's words; a shared byte-for-byte marker fixture) and released as v0.1475.0 with the step B follow-ups: a report about a P2P group goes to its creator as a flagged sealed DM through one narrow relay exception (both in a group the recipient created, 3 a day); the creator's app checks each item against its own copy; Remove changes the group key first (sealed to everyone but the removed person), on both clients. Also BUG-177 (a busy person's automatic reject told a hidden caller they were online; now it rings out with a missed-call line), a refused contact request marked request:true so neither app offers another, the ten-trade limit no longer counting requests sent to you, and the web Trade page (it never signed in) fixed.
recent_decisions.why: Server admins cannot read or check encrypted group messages, nor remove a member; the creator can. Rekeying on removal is what makes Remove mean anything: without it the removed person keeps reading. The follow-ups were in PRIORITIES from steps B and C; each was small and each closed a real leak or a broken page.

recent_decisions.decision: Released v0.1476.0: spec 10k (files in DMs and P2P groups encrypted on both clients, inline display on the desktop, a marker never sent into a public channel), BUG-178 (Pin, Edit and React refused by the relay outside its own rooms, hidden on private rows, and refused at each send point while a private conversation is open), BUG-179 (the desktop log no longer records file markers, which carried keys), and the account words (terminology_lint gains ACCOUNT_SEED; every "seed" meaning the account key changed to "recovery phrase").
recent_decisions.why: Reviewing the safety follow-ups showed private files only as private as their links: a web DM paste and every group file went up as plain public files. The web 10k build then found its group rows offered the server Pin and Edit, which sent group text in the clear (an admin pin would have been kept and broadcast); the desktop build found DM file keys in run.log. Checked the live server read-only: its only two pins are in #general, so nothing private was ever pinned.

recent_decisions.decision: Batch review of the safety arc (three read-only critics, one feature area each) after v0.1476.0; about 30 seam defects confirmed and fixed in three parallel batches with red-first tests: web shipped as v0.1476.1 together with BUG-180 (v0.1476.0 broke web group rows), relay and desktop as v0.1477.0. Highlights: dm_put gets its own burst bucket (8, then 1/s) and both apps pace pass sweeps; Reply bound to its own conversation; removed group members cannot rejoin with an old ticket, epoch keys cannot be overwritten, newest 200 group messages; reported staff never see their reports; protected setup locks groups, invites and friend codes and lives in its own atomic file. Recorded as BUG-181.

The review ran after shipping, which let BUG-180 reach the live site for a few hours; next time the critics run before an arc is called done.

recent_decisions.decision: Spec 10l shipped as v0.1478.0 (relay, web and desktop together, BUG-182): every friendship-pass dm_put carries a random ref; the relay answers dm_put_ok or dm_put_refused {reason} to the sender alone (src/relay/handlers/dm_answer.rs); a pass counts as given only on dm_put_ok, the self-copy waits for it, an unanswered pass is kept as perhaps given (native passes_unanswered, web passesUnsure, at most 4 per friend) and withdrawn with the rest. Exception kept on purpose: an untick (Message, Call or Trade) withdraws the passes allowing it at once, not when the new pass is taken; the friend stays on the People I choose list meanwhile (web passFriends). Same release: a removed group member let back in is sealed to again once a member list asked for after the removal names them; a re-seal ignores members with no Kyber key; the chat limiter no longer subtracts Instants (Windows boot panic); the desktop phrase-lock line draws only its first sentence.
recent_decisions.why: A second review of the batch-review fixes found that pacing only made a refused pass rarer: the relay never said which put it refused, so both apps could show a friendship complete while the friend held no pass. The untick exception follows the earlier rule that consent taken back takes effect now; the desktop builder proposed it and the web took it up with a red-first test. Relay and clients ship together because a client whose ref is never answered records no pass at all.

recent_decisions.decision: v0.1479.0 (BUG-183): the web scratch pad treats files like a private conversation (encrypted upload, marker kept in localStorage by app.js scratchPadKeep) and its rows are private rows (SCRATCH_PAD_ROW: no React, Edit, server Pin or Delete); the desktop is_private_channel counts "scratchpad" so its rows offer none either. The PRIORITIES follow-up line about the scratchpad was removed.
recent_decisions.why: The follow-up list said the scratchpad still uploaded plain files; checking both clients showed the desktop had been fixed in v0.1477.0 but the web never was, and neither client hid the row actions that send a row's words to the server. A follow-up list has to be checked against both mirrors, not just the one that was fixed.

recent_decisions.decision: v0.1480.0 (BUG-184): each app checks its own "who can reach me" setting for calls on an incoming ring (desktop on_ring via DmStore::admits_from, web ringIgnored), ignoring a refused ring like a blocked caller's; with no store or settings loaded the relay's check stands. The desktop DM screen now counts passes still waiting for an answer (passes_held_by), matching the web's passMayHeld.
recent_decisions.why: Closes the step B follow-up "incoming rings are not also filtered by the callee's own app", the same defence the DM screen already gives against a server that passes something on by mistake. Writing it exposed that the desktop half of 10l had not taught the DM screen about unanswered passes, which the web half had.

recent_decisions.decision: v0.1481.0 (BUG-185): the relay stamps each player's identity key beside their name (components.key, and key on game_player_joined); the desktop keeps it on RemotePlayer and skips a blocked key in the figure pass (lib.rs) and nameplate_labels (engine/block.rs hides_player). And components_seen_by_others sends another player only name, appearance and key (PLAYER_FIELDS_SEEN_BY_OTHERS); crew and things keep theirs, a player's own welcome entry keeps all.

Adding it showed that everyone in view was sent each player's health, inventory, experience and quests, which no client read for anyone else, so that went in the same release. The operator checked in mid-work ("it's been like 12 hours") and was given the status.

recent_decisions.decision: Spec 10m (docs/design/blocking-and-safe-mode.md, commit bf8c4c582) written from two read-only critic reviews of v0.1478 to v0.1481, and built by a desktop and a web worktree agent in parallel: R1 a contact request follows only on dm_put_ok (desktop); R2 a re-issue that takes something away sends its self-copy at once and the new pass goes out before the withdrawals; R3 a pass withdrawn by my other device marks the friend "changed on my other device" and is never replaced with the defaults; R4 an untick always takes back unanswered passes (desktop); R5 echo guard (desktop); R6 one send per friend and Unfollow drops a waiting send (desktop); R7 a pass refused for reach is not resent on its own; R8 group membership in the apps own DM/ring checks is the relay call; R9 HUD co-presence list skips blocked players; R10 scratch pad: no typing indicator, desktop keeps entries in the encrypted DM store, web command rows private, reply kept, labels accurate.
recent_decisions.why: The worst finding re-granted a withdrawn permission across two devices of one person (holding the self-copy until dm_put_ok meant the other device never learned an untick whose new pass was refused, then minted the defaults). Next worst: the new ring check could drop a call the person allowed because each app reads a stale group list. Fail safe is the rule: a device that did not see the choice never gives back what was withdrawn.

recent_decisions.decision: v0.1482.0 (BUG-186): spec 10m merged from both halves and aligned (the web's refused-echo list taken to the desktop; the desktop's withdraw-in-flight-passes-when-marking taken to the web). Plus a leak found while checking: the desktop history pump asked /api/messages?channel=dm:<key> on opening a DM; now only a server's own rooms (net_route::history_channel). Live server checked read-only: 3 nginx lines in the oldest rotated log (ages out within a day), none in the relay journal; nothing deleted.
recent_decisions.why: Multi-device consent must never widen by itself; and the sealed-sender design is undone if the client tells the server whose conversation it opened. Deleting the 3 log lines would be an operator call; they rotate out on their own.

recent_decisions.decision: Spec 10n (commit 91ac73d78): the choice for each friend syncs as its own signed self-note [[hum:choice:v1]]<key>/<may> (newer at wins, equal at: larger may text), the block-notes pattern; passes follow the choice on every device (withdraw beyond at once, echoes never change the choice); 10m R2 withdrawn (self-copies held until dm_put_ok again, refused-echo lists removed); offline Unfollow queued; sweep waits for the mailbox on connect; web scratch pad into the encrypted DM store. Desktop and web built in parallel worktrees.
recent_decisions.why: A third critic, reviewing 10m, found more two-device orderings that lost or reversed a choice (an offline untick undone from the web; a marked friend re-granted with one click; an older echo winning). All share one root: ticks rebuilt from pass echoes that arrive late, out of order or never. Patching orderings one by one does not converge; syncing the choice itself as state, like the block list, does.

recent_decisions.decision: v0.1483.0 (BUG-187): spec 10n merged from both halves. The web settled the open details (Unfollow clears as of its signed time, Block regardless; choices survive a server identity change; sweep targets mutual follows and existing pass holders; a tick always succeeds once the store is loaded; contact-request echo under the pass echo rule; 128-bit applied-note hashes) and the desktop matched them. A narrow parity critic ran on the merge.
recent_decisions.why: One spec, two builders, the web going first on details; the parity critic is the last check that both apps reach the same state for the same events.

recent_decisions.decision: v0.1513.0: MP4 (H.264/AAC, and anything else Windows decodes) plays in the desktop player through Windows Media Foundation (src/media/system.rs): media::probe tries our Matroska/AV1 path first, then the system path; the decode thread and kira sound mirror the AV1 path's queue/generation/seek rules. I figure this simplified version of interacting with machines, pipes, cables, etc. would be a lot easier for people to digest. We could say it's augmented reality. What we design could literally be used to AR whenever I can afford AR glasses. This is how we can justify the constellation lines we added to the skybox and real star catalog. recent_decisions.why: Operator, verbatim: "We should go with what people would experience in the real world. I guess that means we should add a way of changing the material of the pipe/cable/tube/whatever. The spline/line/edge/vertex whatever should be easy to move.
